title: Spread: range, IQR and standard deviation
hook: Spread is about how far values sit from the center, not how big they are.

steps.prompt: From memory: what does a larger standard deviation tell you?
steps.answer: The values are more spread out from the mean.

steps.prompt: Which list has the larger standard deviation? A: 10, 10, 10, 10. B: 1, 10, 19, 10.
steps.why: A has no spread at all.

steps.prompt: For each pair, which list has the larger standard deviation?
steps.why: Standard deviation measures distance from the mean. Values far from the center mean more spread.

steps.prompt: Adding 5 to every value in a data set does what to the standard deviation?
steps.why: Everything shifts together, so the distances from the mean don't change.

steps.prompt: A box plot has $Q1 = 12$, median 18 and $Q3 = 25$. What's the interquartile range?
Two classes have the same mean score. Class X's scores bunch near the mean; Class Y's are spread out. Tap the false statement.
lines: Class Y has the larger standard deviation
Class X most likely has the smaller range
Class X must have the higher median
Both classes have the same mean
steps.why: Spread says nothing certain about the median.

steps.prompt: Multiplying every value by 3 does what to the standard deviation?
steps.why: Every distance from the mean triples.

keys: Standard deviation measures spread around the mean.
Adding a constant: no change in spread. Multiplying: spread scales too.

recall.why: How far values are from the mean.
